summary: Jelu is a self-hosted reading tracker designed to help you organise your current books and maintain a to-read list. It provides a centralised web interface to log your reading habits, monitor progress, and catalogue personal libraries. Released under the MIT licence, the project is built using Java and is distributed via Docker.
goodFor: This is a suitable tool for someone who wants a dedicated, self-hosted system to manage a personal reading list without relying on third-party commercial platforms.
watchOut: The project has a moderate maintenance profile and overlaps heavily with widely adopted alternatives in the media tracking space, meaning community support may be relatively niche.
deployNotes: Because the application is packaged as a Docker container running Java, you will typically need to map persistent storage volumes for your data and place it behind a reverse proxy to handle TLS termination.
